Build an Attention-Weighted Transition Network (ATNA)

Source: R/estimate_network.R
build_atna.Rd

build_atna() estimates an attention-weighted transition network (ATNA): every later state in a sequence, not only the next one, adds to the edge from an earlier state, with a weight that decays with the number of positions between them, exp(-distance / lambda). It is build_network() with method = "attention". The decay is set in params: lambda (default 1; larger values decay more slowly) and direction ("forward", the default, "backward" or "both"). duration (one value per position, accumulated into times) or time_matrix (one row per sequence, one column per position) measure the distance in time instead of positions, and decay, a function of (ti, tj, lambda) returning one weight per pair, replaces the decay function.

The weights are summed decay weights, not counts or probabilities, so they compare within one network; add scaling = "normalize" for rows that sum to 1. Check how far they move under resampling with bootstrap_network().

Usage

build_atna(
  data,
  start = FALSE,
  end = FALSE,
  actor = NULL,
  action = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  session = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

The sequences: a data frame with one row per sequence and one column per position, or an event log (one row per event, with action set). Column roles are declared as in build_network(). One-hot data and matrices are refused.

start

A start state put before every sequence, so the network shows where sequences begin. FALSE (default) adds none, TRUE adds one labelled "Start", a single string adds one with that label.

end

An end state put after each sequence's last observed state, so the network shows where sequences stop; it has no outgoing edges. FALSE (default), TRUE ("End") or a single string, as start.

actor

The column naming who each row belongs to (a person, a team). In an event log, each actor's events form a sequence, split further by session or time_threshold. Default NULL.

action

The column holding each event's state; setting it declares the data an event log. Column names give no role: action, actor, time and session are read only when set. A column called Action with nothing declared raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input, and an undeclared time or session column beside action is named in a message of class nestimate_column_role. Default NULL.

time

The timestamp column of an event log. Events are ordered by it, and a gap longer than time_threshold starts a new sequence. Default NULL.

session

The column identifying sessions in an event log; each session is its own sequence, also without actor. Default NULL.

...

Further arguments for build_network(), such as group, params, scaling, threshold or state_cols. method cannot be given: it is always "attention" (error of class nestimate_bad_input).

Value

A netobject (a netobject_group with group), exactly as build_network() returns it: print it for an overview, read the edges with extract_edges() and the weights with extract_transition_matrix(), and draw it with cograph::splot().

See also

build_network

Examples

net <- build_atna(trajectories)
net
